I wonder if it would be cleaner to inject a parameter with default implementation such as `supportedThreats: [ThreatKind] = ThreatKind.allCases`. Then on the client we would set to [.phishing, .malware] if `isScamProtectionEnabled` is disabled. 

Reasons are: 
- `isMaliciousSiteProtectionEnabled` feature flag is checked on the client side while `isScamProtectionEnabled` is checked here. I know they are two different use case but we could leave the library unaware of the feature flag.
- Simplified tests as we don’t have to inject mocks.
- If for example we add another layer of protection such as `fakeNews` sites protection and we put it under another feature flag then this code
`for threatKind in supportedThreats` would stay the same while this
```
if !isScamProtectionEnabled && threatKind == .scam {
  return .none
}
```
would just be `if !supportedThreats.contains(threatKind) { return .none }` and stay the same for any type of unsupported threats.

But this may be a personal preference, nothing wrong with your approach. Just food for thought.
